newsitem.title: UK: BP's first-quarter results beat forecasts.
newsitem.headline: BP's first-quarter results beat forecasts.

text.p: British Petroleum Co. Plc said Tuesday that higher oil prices, increased volumes and cost reductions had enabled it to record first-quarter results well ahead of market forecasts.

BP said its net income before exceptional items rose by 19 percent to 755 million pounds ($1.2 billion) from 633 million ($1.02 billion) a year ago. In dollar terms, earnings in the quarter rose by 27 percent.
BP shares rose strongly after the earnings report, which beat expectations centred around 690 million pounds ($1.12 billion).
Analysts noted that the performance was strong across BP's range of operations.

"The results are very good ... better in every segment," said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analyst Paul Spedding. "It's important to note that it's not just (higher) oil prices -- it's also refining and chemicals."

The company said its improving portfolio of assets, its continuing focus on costs and its reduced level of debt were lowering the impact of changes in prices and margins, and said progress towards its medium-term targets remained ahead of schedule.
It said higher oil prices and volumes led to a 24 percent increase in upstream earnings to a record 913 million pounds ($1.48 billion), a 32 percent rise in dollar terms.

In chemicals, however, the result was down by 19 percent, reflecting the effect of the strong pound sterling and lower underlying margins, but BP said the outcome still represented an 18 percent return on capital.
BP said its oil and gas production rose by 3.5 percent in the quarter to a six-year high thanks to increased output from fields commissioned last year.
Combined oil and gas output rose to 1.601 million barrels of oil equivalent per day from 1.546 million in the first quarter of 1996, it said.
